hook: This is a loud comedy article about HOGSLICE, an all-caps forum troll who, if you argue back, may physically show up at your house looking like wrestler Scott Steiner and put you in the hospital. Expect constant profanity, crude sexual insults and slapstick beatings with broken bones, all laid out in mock forum threads and subreddit pages. If the swearing does not bother you, the escalation is a lot of fun.
whyItMatters: It takes a very familiar online figure, the aggressive reply guy who picks fights on hobby boards, and gives him a literal body with consequences. The joke is that the Foundation answers a cartoon bully with full procedure: tracking software, Veil cover-ups, and a containment log of failed traps. It also brings in Agent Woodcock and his haunted knife SCP-5175, set up through a crosslinked file, for a staged showdown.
thingsToNotice: The early incidents are escalating sketches matched to each board: a cryptid fan who prefers the crying Squonk gets his skull and femurs broken, a Muppet collector is clubbed unconscious with a banjo while HOGSLICE sings an insulting Rainbow Connection, and a Japanese bug-fighting moderator is buried under his own insects and elbow-dropped. Tranquilizers and an electrified room both fail, so Woodcock fights him in the dark like a wrestling match, and the two keep stopping to bond over tattoos, the Joker and how cool the knife's skeletal spirit is. When Woodcock finally stabs him, HOGSLICE praises him as the first opponent who kept up, drives the blade deeper himself to be finished properly, and vanishes in purple mist while Woodcock tears up. The twist is that he survives: the accounts return the next day posting only on therapy and self-help boards, asking how to grow grass, how to calm down, and saying he wants a friend and a therapist, then go silent. Two years later an email arrives saying he quit the internet, joined a biker gang on a Harley, and would get a beer with the knife guy, now signed HOGNICE.

related.note: The knife Agent Woodcock wields in the showdown; this file points to it for how the two became bound.
